lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
For recipe and scale problems, solve a guided problem with visible working and a one-sentence reason for the method.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: method named, working complete, result checked for reasonableness.

WATCH FOR
Skipping working for recipe and scale problems, or mixing units/places without checking.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.explain:
Stage 4 Mathematics develops fluent reasoning for recipe and scale problems. Students choose a valid method, show working, and check reasonableness. Catalogue alignment uses MA4-ARI-C-01. Prefer exact reasoning over guessing.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Skipping working for recipe and scale problems, or mixing units/places without checking. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
